Text:
# NATIVE VALVE ENDOCARDITIS WITH STREPTOCOCCI

Selection is based on susceptibility to penicillin.

# Treatment of Streptococci pneumonia, Streptococcus pyogenes, and Groups B, C, F and G beta-hemolytic streptococci

Treatment is non-standardized and must be tailored to each patient. Consult Infectious Diseases.

---

References:

- Baddour et al., Circulation 2015, 132:1-52
- Mandell chapter: Endocarditis and intravascular infections
- Sanford keyword: Endocarditis
- Up-To-Date article: Overview of management of infective endocarditis in adults
- Wang et al., JAMA 2018, 320.1:72-83
Therapy:
## Treatment of highly susceptible viridians streptococci or Streptococcus gallolyticus (bovis) (penicillin MIC less than or equal to 0.12 mcg/ml)

The addition of gentamicin provides a synergistic effect and is reasonable to add in patients with uncomplicated endocarditis, rapid response to therapy and no underlying renal disease

Preferred:

Penicillin G 3 million units IV q4h ($$) R for 4 weeks

< OR >

Penicillin G 3 million units IV q4h ($$) R for 2 weeks <AND> gentamicin

3 mg/kg IV q24h ($) [R,O] for 2 weeks

Primary alternatives:

[Assessment of beta-lactam reaction CLICK HERE](beta-lactam-allergy-assessment)

Ceftriaxone 2 gm IV q24h ($) M for 4 weeks

< OR >

Ceftriaxone 2 gm IV q24h ($) for 2 weeks <AND> gentamicin 3 mg/kg IV once
daily ($) [R,O] for 2 weeks

Secondary alternative, after assessment of beta-lactam reaction above:

Vancomycin 15 mg/kg IV q12h ($) R for 4 weeks

## Treatment of relatively resistant viridians streptococci or S. gallolyticus (bovis) (penicillin MIC greater than 0.12 and less than or equal to 0.5 mcg/ml)

For ceftriaxone susceptible isolates (MIC < 0.5 mcg/mL):

Ceftriaxone 2 gm IV q24h ($) for 4 weeks

For ceftriaxone resistant isolates (MIC >/= 0.5 mcg/mL):

Penicillin G 4 million units IV q4h ($$) R for 4 weeks <AND> gentamicin

3 mg/kg IV q24h ($) [R,O] for first 2 weeks

< OR >

Ceftriaxone 2 gm IV q24h ($) for 4 weeks <AND> gentamicin 3 mg/kg IV q24h

($) [R,O] for first 2 weeks

Alternative:

[Assessment of beta-lactam reaction CLICK HERE](beta-lactam-allergy-assessment)

Vancomycin 15 mg/kg IV q12h ($) R for 4 weeks

## Treatment of highly resistant viridians streptococci or S. gallolyticus (bovis) (penicillin MIC greater than or equal to 0.5 mcg/mL)

Preferred:

Penicillin G 4 million units IV q4h ($$) R <AND> gentamicin 1 mg/kg IV q24h

($) [R,O] for 4 weeks

< OR>

Ampicillin 2 gm IV q4h ($$) R <AND> gentamicin 1 mg/kg IV q8h ($) R,O
for 4 weeks

Alternative:

[Assessment of beta-lactam reaction CLICK HERE](beta-lactam-allergy-assessment)

Vancomycin 15 mg/kg IV q12h ($) R for 4 weeks
